name: Underhand T-Bar Row
description: The underhand T-bar row uses a supinated (palms-up) grip on the T-bar, allowing the elbows to track close to the body and placing the biceps in a mechanically advantageous position. The supinated grip enables a fuller range of motion and facilitates lower lat engagement at the bottom of the pull, making it a popular choice for developing lower lat thickness.

execution.starting_position: Straddle the T-bar machine. Turn the hands supinated (palms up) on the handles or bar. Hinge to 45-60 degrees, arms extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Some T-bar machines do not accommodate a supinated grip — in that case, use a straight bar end on a landmine setup where the hands can grip palm-up.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended, palms facing up.
Step 2: Initiate the row by driving the elbows back alongside the torso.
Step 3: Pull until the elbows pass torso level.
Step 4: Squeeze at the top, feeling the lower lats contract.
Step 5: Lower under control to full arm extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Supinating the wrists so far it becomes uncomfortable — find a comfortable angle
Bicep-dominant pulling — think lat stretch and contraction, not curl
safety_considerations: The supinated wrist position can stress the wrist joint — progress load conservatively
Avoid this variation with wrist injuries
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to full lat contraction.
coaching_cues: Feel the stretch under the arms at the bottom
